subject: Re: Data residency / region pinning - next steps
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Data residency follow-up (EU pinning)

Thanks for the call earlier, Marissa - good to meet the Redwood team. A quick recap from my side and a few open questions we promised to surface to our security/compliance team:

- Priority: Acme Bank requires customer data residency in the EU for any production workloads that process EU customer PII. We are evaluating region pinning vs. self-hosted private deployments.
- Failover: We need deterministic cross-region failover behavior - if eu-west-1 is unavailable, what happens to new requests? Will traffic fail to a US region? We need an option to opt out of cross-region failover (no cross-border data movement) except for explicit backups.
- Backups & snapshots: Where are nightly backups stored by default? Can we ensure backups remain in EU? Also need encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Logging/PII: Audit logs and request/response logging - we need to know which logs contain PII, retention windows (we prefer 13 months), and whether logs can be redacted or disabled.

Next steps from our side: our security team will send a formal questionnaire, but would appreciate a written summary of Redwood's region pinning and failover semantics, plus any template DPA/SLA you can provide.

Thanks,
Sanjay
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Bank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmebank.com>

Hi Sanjay - great speaking with you as well. Per our discussion, here is a high-level summary and proposed next steps (I kept it focused so you can share directly with your security/compliance folks):

High-level answers
- Region pinning: Redwood supports account- and route-level region pinning. You can pin the production route to eu-west-1 (Ireland) so inference traffic and model state (KV cache) are served from that region.
- Failover behavior: We support configurable failover policies:
  - strict: no cross-region failover (requests are dropped/queued with alerts) - guarantees zero cross-border request servicing
  - tolerant: automatic failover to a specified secondary region (e.g., us-east-1) for availability
  - queued-failover: queue requests for a short window (configurable) before failing to a secondary region
- Backups: Snapshots and backups can be configured to remain in the pinned region. By default we replicate backups to a designated secondary region for durability, but for regulated customers we offer an option to restrict backups to the primary region only.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations and an HSM-backed option for Private deployments.
- Logging & retention: Audit logs include coarse metadata about requests by default. Sensitive payload logging (full request/response) is disabled by default for regulated customers; we can enable redaction or per-route logging control. Retention is configurable - we typically support 90/180/365/400+ day retention tiers; 13 months (395 days) is available via a custom retention policy.

Attachments: I attached our data residency whitepaper and a short data mapping template your team can fill out (acme-data-mapping-template.xlsx).

Proposed next steps
1) We'll provide a short technical deep-dive with Aditya (infra) to walk through architecture and failover knobs - please propose a 60-min slot next week.
2) Please share the security questionnaire when you have it; we'll aim to return answers + SOC 2 report + DPA in ~3 business days.
3) Confirm preferred primary region (eu-west-1) and whether backups must remain in-region.

Happy to loop in our Compliance lead if needed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Data residency follow-up (EU pinning)

Marissa - thanks for the summary. A few concrete items our security/compliance team needs clarified before we move to a POC:

1) Backups location and segregation:
   - If backups are replicated to a secondary region by default, can that behavior be disabled? We need written confirmation that backups can be restricted to EU only.
2) Encryption keys:
   - We require customer-managed KMS for production encryption keys. Is there an option to bring our key (BYOK) and rotate it on our schedule?
3) Audit logs and PII isolation:
   - Please provide a list of log types (access, request, response, system) and indicate which contain full request/response data.
   - Can request/response data be configured to be redacted at ingestion?
4) Cross-border failover policy:
   - We need a deterministic SLA behavior description: in strict mode, will requests be rejected with 5xx or queued? What observability signals are available to detect region failover events?

Deliverables requested:
- SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent evidence
- DPA template and draft language for data residency clauses
- Short doc describing failover semantics + sample config snippet for route policy

CC'ing Aditya since he offered a deeper technical session.

Thanks,
Elena
Security Architect - Acme Bank
